A_target.statement:
Let $x = \sqbrk {\overline {a_0; a_1, \ldots, a_{k - 1} } }$ be a [[Definition:Periodic Continued Fraction|purely periodic continued fraction]] with $a_i \in \Z_{>0}$.
Then $x$ is a [[Definition:Quadratic Irrational|quadratic irrational]] satisfying an explicit quadratic equation with [[Definition:Integer|integer]] coefficients.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map M z = \dfrac {a z + b} {c z + d}$ be a [[Definition:Möbius Transformation|Möbius transformation]].
Then its [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed points]] are the roots of:
:$c z^2 + \paren {d - a} z - b = 0$

substitutions.the Mobius transformation: the composite of the k partial-quotient maps z -> a_i + 1/z
substitutions.the fixed point of the transformation: the value of the periodic continued fraction
substitutions.the coefficient matrix: the product of the partial-quotient matrices

derived.the fixed-point quadratic: the minimal polynomial of the quadratic irrational

object_map.reformulation: The infinite continued fraction must be reformulated as a self-referential finite expression before it can be read as a fixed-point equation.

validity_conditions: the continued fraction must be purely periodic so the composite map returns to the same expression
the partial quotients must be positive integers so the composite matrix has integer entries and determinant +-1
the relevant root must be selected by positivity, since the quadratic has two roots and only one is the limit
proof_plan:
Write one period as a composite of the maps:
:$\map {T_i} z = a_i + \dfrac 1 z$

Each $T_i$ is represented by the [[Definition:Integer|integer]] [[Definition:Matrix|matrix]] $\begin {pmatrix} a_i & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end {pmatrix}$.
The product:
:$\begin {pmatrix} p_{k - 1} & p_{k - 2} \\ q_{k - 1} & q_{k - 2} \end {pmatrix} = \displaystyle \prod_{i \mathop = 0}^{k - 1} \begin {pmatrix} a_i & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end {pmatrix}$
represents $M = T_0 \circ \cdots \circ T_{k - 1}$.

By periodicity:
:$x = \map M x = \dfrac {p_{k - 1} x + p_{k - 2} } {q_{k - 1} x + q_{k - 2} }$

Clearing denominators:
:$q_{k - 1} x^2 + \paren {q_{k - 2} - p_{k - 1} } x - p_{k - 2} = 0$
which is a quadratic with [[Definition:Integer|integer]] coefficients.
